correctness.rationale: Diagonalization reduces classical constant-step FISTA on an SPD quadratic to independent scalar modes. The first four modal polynomials are derived directly from the published recurrence. The first three comparisons are nonexpansive because 1<a<2. The fourth comparison factors into q times one linear and one quadratic factor; their root ordering proves that objective increase occurs exactly on one open normalized-curvature band. Intersecting that band with [1/kappa,1] gives the exact universal frontier. The packaged checker independently replays all constants and the kappa=4/3 witness.

value.rationale: Ordinary FISTA is widely used and its nonmonotone objective traces motivated a dedicated monotone variant. The new result turns that qualitative fact into a natural complete early-iteration classification: it proves the first three completed steps cannot increase an SPD quadratic objective, identifies exactly when the fourth can, and shows the phenomenon already at condition number 4/3 with a nearly sixfold jump. This sharp low-conditioning boundary is useful for interpreting objective traces and for understanding why monotonicity safeguards can activate even on benign quadratic problems.
